Samsung OM75S(31) is a compact digital signage display module released by Samsung Electronics in 2018. It features a 75-inch diagonal screen with 4K UHD resolution (3840 x 2160 pixels) and is designed for commercial and enterprise applications. The display uses Samsung's proprietary quantum dot technology for enhanced color accuracy and deeper blacks.

The OM75S(31) includes built-in Wi-Fi connectivity and Samsung's Tizen operating system, allowing for easy content management and remote monitoring. It has a brightness rating of 500 nits and a contrast ratio of 4000:1, making it suitable for well-lit indoor environments.

The module is particularly popular in retail settings, corporate lobbies, and educational institutions due to its slim profile (less than 30mm depth) and versatile mounting options. It features multiple input ports including HDMI 2.0, DisplayPort 1.2, and USB, along with RS-232C control for integration with external control systems.

One of its standout features is the ability to operate 24/7 with a maximum power consumption of just 180 watts, thanks to its advanced power management system and LED backlighting. The display also incorporates Samsung's Advanced Color Management System, which automatically adjusts color temperature based on ambient lighting conditions and maintains consistent image quality throughout its 50,000-hour rated lifespan.

It is particularly notable for its groundbreaking use of quantum heating technology, which allows it to cook food almost instantaneously. This model also features a marble-coated interior, which is meant to provide better heat distribution and is easier to clean compared to the common ceramic or stainless steel interiors found in other microwaves. The OM75S(31) boasts a 5000-watt output, making it one of the most powerful domestic microwaves available. Additionally, its digital interface includes a holographic display, which was quite avant-garde for appliances of that time.

The Samsung OM75S(31) is a microwave magnetron tube that was widely used in Samsung microwave ovens during the late 1990s and early 2000s. This component was known for its reliability and efficient power conversion, typically operating at 2.45 GHz frequency, which is standard for microwave cooking applications.

The OM75S(31) could generate approximately 750 watts of cooking power while drawing about 1100 watts from the power supply. Its design featured a cylindrical permanent magnet and a copper anode cavity, which was innovative for its time. The magnetron utilized a thoriated tungsten filament cathode, which provided good electron emission at relatively low temperatures.

One of the distinguishing features of the OM75S(31) was its improved cooling system, which incorporated aluminum heat sinks and allowed for better heat dissipation compared to previous models. This design helped extend the component's lifespan to approximately 2,000 hours of operation.

The model gained popularity in Asian markets particularly because its compact design allowed for smaller microwave oven cabinets, which was ideal for apartments in densely populated urban areas. Production of the OM75S(31) continued until 2008, when it was gradually replaced by the more energy-efficient OM85P series, which featured a platinum-coated cathode and ceramic magnets.
